# Before you start

RiboPilot runs its analysis inside a container: Docker on a workstation, or
Singularity (also called Apptainer) on a computing cluster. The container holds
every analysis tool, so you do not install them yourself.

RiboPilot is developed and tested on Linux. On a Mac it needs Docker Desktop;
Apple Silicon Macs run the container through emulation, which is slower. On
Windows, use WSL2 and run R inside WSL. On a cluster, use Singularity or
Apptainer (see [Running on a cluster](Clusters.html)).

**Disk space.** The container image is about 2.6 GB to download and 7.7 GB on
disk. Each project also needs room for its own files: the test project
used 1.6 GB, mostly Nextflow's working files (0.9 GB) and the taxonomy copy
(0.5 GB). Reference databases are small: the two built for the test
project took 4 MB and 16 MB.
[Disk space, caches, and offline use](Caches-and-Offline.html) says where
each of these goes, and how to move it.

# Install the tools

Install each of these once, and check it with the command beside it.

1. **Docker** (workstation). On Linux, add yourself to the `docker` group so
   Docker runs without `sudo`. On a Mac, start Docker Desktop. Check:
   `docker run hello-world`. On a cluster, use **Singularity** or
   **Apptainer** instead. Check: `singularity --version`.
2. **Java** 17 or newer. Check: `java -version`.
3. **[Nextflow](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/install.html)**, a version
   from 24.10 through 25.10. Check: `nextflow -v`. If you have a newer
   Nextflow, RiboPilot runs version 25.10.6 instead, downloading it once. To set
   this yourself, add `export NXF_VER=25.10.6` to your shell profile.
4. **[R](https://www.r-project.org/)** 4.4.0 or newer. Check: `R --version`.
5. **RiboPilot**, in R:

   ```r
   install.packages("remotes")
   remotes::install_github("dmacguigan/RiboPilot")
   ```

::: {.alert .alert-info}
**Private preview.** While the RiboPilot repository is private, installing it
and downloading the test reads need a GitHub personal access token. Put
`GITHUB_PAT=<your token>` in your `~/.Renviron` file (in R,
`usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens it), then restart R.
:::

# Check that it works

Run the test project: see [Get started](RiboPilot.html). It exercises every
tool above, and the first run downloads the container image.

# Optional: an NCBI API key

An [NCBI API key](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/docs/v2/api/api-keys/) lets
RiboPilot query NCBI faster. It is free. The simplest place for it is your
`~/.Renviron` file, next to any other keys:

```
NCBI_API_KEY=<your key>
```

Restart R after you edit the file. RiboPilot then passes the key to every run
and every reference build, without writing it into the project's `.config`
file. You can instead pass it to `RiboPilot::new_project()` as `ncbi_api_key`;
it is then stored in the project's `.config` file and shows in the Nextflow
command of the run window.

Never paste your key into a screenshot, an email, or an issue.

# Upgrading RiboPilot

Run these in R, one step at a time:

```r
# 1. Remove the installed RiboPilot
remove.packages("RiboPilot")

# 2. Restart R
#    RStudio: Session > Restart R, or run rstudioapi::restartSession()
#    Elsewhere: quit R and start it again

# 3. Install the new version
remotes::install_github("dmacguigan/RiboPilot")

# 4. Update each existing project, once per project
RiboPilot::backwards_compatibility("~/my_project")
```

The [changelog](https://dmacguigan.github.io/RiboPilot/news/index.html) lists
what changed.

Step 4 brings the project's database up to date and points the project at the
container image for the RiboPilot you installed. The next run downloads that
image by itself, so there is nothing to pull by hand. Your samples, results,
and settings are kept. Before it changes anything, RiboPilot saves a copy of
the database (`.sqlite.bak.<timestamp>`) and of the project's `.config`
(`.config.bak.<timestamp>`) in the project folder. To see what would change
without changing anything, add `dry_run = TRUE`.

What you see if you skip this step:

- **The database is out of date.** The app does not open, and says "This
  project needs an update. Run backwards_compatibility(...) first."
- **Only the container image is out of date.** The app opens and says
  "Container version does not match RiboPilot". Runs still work, with the code
  and tools in the older image.

Projects made before RiboPilot 0.1.0 cannot be updated. Make a new project with
`new_project()`, in a new folder, from the same mapping file and reads.
Reference databases in your reference folder are kept and reused.

Each image takes about 7.7 GB in Docker, or about 2.5 GB as a Singularity
file. Once no project uses an old one, remove it with
`docker image rm <image>`; with Singularity, delete its file from your image
cache (see [Disk space, caches, and offline use](Caches-and-Offline.html)).
